subject: Finalizing AP route & card exception timeline — Redwing Health
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@redwinghealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — AP route options / next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side after the call: 

What we heard
- Redwing wants a predictable commercial path for production usage (pilot -> production).
- Preference: vendor-friendly PO process for larger commitments, but card possible for pilot/POC to speed start.
- Procurement will require vendor onboarding (W-9, insurance proof, SOC2 summary) before final PO.

Options we can support
1) PO-first (standard enterprise path) — Redwood issues invoice net30 after PO acceptance; vendor onboarding checklist (7–10 business days typical).
2) Card-for-pilot (accelerated) — one-time card or virtual card payment; requires billing contact and corporate card exception approval on your side.
3) Marketplace (if you want procurement via cloud marketplace) — we can enable marketplace billing; onboarding varies by marketplace and may change SLAs/costs.

Attachments: commercial-path-options.pdf (summary + estimated timelines).

Asks / next steps
- Can you confirm which route Procurement prefers for the initial pilot? (PO or card)
- Please share the vendor onboarding contact (name/email) so we can start the paperwork in parallel.
- If PO, any internal PO templates we should expect, and an estimated approval lead time?

I'll loop in Marissa on PO/finance logistics and Aditya for technical billing requirements. If it helps, we can draft a short MOP (mutual action plan) that lists onboarding tasks and owners.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min follow-up with procurement if that moves things faster.

Best,
Olga
Senior Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: commercial-path-options.pdf (3 pages, summary table)

From: Samir Khan <samir.k@redwinghealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Redwing Procurement <procurement@redwinghealth.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — AP route options / next steps

Olga — thanks for the clear notes. Quick answers from procurement + sourcing: 

- For a pilot under $25k we can typically use a corporate card (procurement has a delegated card approval for pilots). For any committed annual spend > $50k they will insist on PO.
- Marketplace: we prefer marketplace for third-party SaaS when available (easier purchase order and internal tracking), but not all vendors are listed yet. If Redwood is on the (Redwing) marketplace, procurement will default there.
- Vendor onboarding: please send W-9, SOC2 letter, proof of insurance and bank wiring instructions. Procurement@redwinghealth will be the owner (I copied them).

Estimated timelines: card payment — same day (once card is authorized); PO path — 7–14 business days (depends on CFO review).

We'd like Redwood to start the vendor onboarding checklist in parallel while we decide PO vs card. Can Marissa or Aditya begin?

Thanks — Samir
Director, Vendor Management
Redwing Health

Thanks Samir — looping in our finance and onboarding owners to start the paperwork. 

Marissa / Aditya / Karthik — Samir confirmed Procurement will own the PO decision; pilot under $25k can run on card. They prefer marketplace if we have a listing. Procurement contact is procurement@redwinghealth.com. Requested onboarding items: W-9, SOC2 summary, COI (insurance), bank details. Samir also asked for an estimated PO approval lead time (he called out 7–14 business days).

Proposed mutual action plan (high level) — would appreciate if one of you can confirm owners and target dates: 
- Redwood: send vendor onboarding packet (W-9, SOC2 summary, COI, wiring) — owner: Marissa — target: EOD Wed 9/9
- Redwood: confirm marketplace presence and provide marketplace enrollment next steps — owner: Karthik — target: 9/10
- Redwing: confirm pilot payment route (card vs PO) — owner: Samir / Procurement — target: 9/10
- Redwood: prepare preview SOW and draft invoice/terms for PO flow — owner: Aditya — target: 9/11

Attachments I am adding: vendor-onboarding-checklist.xlsx, redwood-terms-preview.pdf.

If that timeline looks tight on your side, suggest we push the PO targets by a week — but starting onboarding in parallel will help shorten the go-live. Also, Samir: if you want, we can issue a short one-page statement of work and a DocuSign link for a card payment pilot while procurement completes PO onboarding.

Let me know who takes which item and I will track in HubSpot.

Best,
Olga

Subject: Fwd: Finalizing AP route & card exception timeline — Redwing Health

Samir / Procurement team — looping in a single point from Redwood to accelerate onboarding. Summary of next steps and a couple clarifying asks below.

What Redwood will provide today (sent):
- Completed W-9, SOC2 summary, COI, and bank wiring instructions (see attachments in Olga's email).
- Draft SOW + preview invoice if you choose PO flow (Aditya has the draft ready).

Clarifying asks from Procurement that will unblock PO path:
- Billing address and exact legal entity name to populate on the PO (we need the 8-digit vendor code if you require it).
- Any PO template or required fields (PO reference number format, GL code if applicable).

Card pilot path (if you want to accelerate):
- We can accept a single virtual card charge for pilot setup. Card payments are immediate; accounting will still require vendor onboarding paperwork on file.

Recommendation: start marketplace check in parallel (Karthik will confirm marketplace status tomorrow). If procurement prefers marketplace and enrollment is possible, that will be the fastest path for PO tracking.

Samir — once you confirm billing entity and whether marketplace is required, we will: (1) send DocuSign for the pilot SOW (card) OR (2) wait for PO and issue invoice once PO is routed. Estimated PO onboarding 7–10 business days after vendor packet submitted.

Thanks — Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
